newsitem.title: UK: UK Radio Authority asseses Capital-Virgin deal.
newsitem.headline: UK Radio Authority asseses Capital-Virgin deal.

text.p: Britain's Radio Authority said on Thursday it saw no reason to disallow the proposed acquisition of Virgin Radio, part of Richard Branson's Virgin Group, by Capital Radio.
Capital Radio agreed to take over Virgin Radio for 65 million stg in May in a deal expected to push Capital to a formidable position in Britain's sprawling commercial radio industry.
The acquisition would give Capital three licenses in London --Capital FM, Capital Gold (AM) and Virgin FM -- in addition to one national AM license.
Capital Radio had promised certain undertakings as part of the take-over which the Radio Authority said gave it no reason to disallow the acquisition.

The Authority, however, remained a step away from its final determination until the Office of Fair Trading completed its full probe on the deal's impact on competition in Britain's competition industry.
"...The Authority will make no final determination until the decision of the president of the Board of Trade is known," the Radio Authority said.
Capital Radio's share price rose six pence to 496p after the Authority expressed its views.
